extracted.intended_audience: researchers, grant applicants, institutional research administrators, and small businesses seeking NIH funding
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize and classify the major categories of NIH funding so applicants can find appropriate funding mechanisms and programs that match their needs (training, research, construction, small business, supplements, contracts, prizes, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope Note
rubrics_metrics.description: At any given time, NIH has over 1,000 active funding opportunities that use various funding instruments and announce a broad range of programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explore these categories for insight into the funding landscape and discover programs that may address your needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Training and Career Development
rubrics_metrics.description: Training and career support for scientists, fellows, and trainees at the undergraduate, predoctoral, postdoctoral, early career, and mid-career levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers individual fellowships (F), individual career development awards (K), institutional training (T), research education programs, institutional career development and other training — useful for applicants seeking support for career-stage–specific training and development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research and Development
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH supports a wide variety of research and development programs, including capacity building, conferences and meetings, research projects (small, large, exploratory, pilots), and resource programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes funding for different sizes and types of research projects and resources; useful when looking for mechanisms for exploratory work, pilot studies, larger projects, or shared resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction and Modernization
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH enhances biomedical research through support for construction, renovation, and modernization of new or existing physical infrastructure, e.g., buildings, facilities, laboratories, and fixed equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targeted at institutions seeking capital support for research infrastructure and fixed equipment to enable or expand research capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small Business
rubrics_metrics.description: Support for U.S. small businesses (including minority-, women-, veteran-owned and HUBZone companies) to stimulate technological innovation, pursue research and development, and commercialize biomedical products in NIH areas of science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes SBIR/STTR and other small-business-focused mechanisms; intended for U.S.-based small businesses aiming to translate research into commercial products or technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental Funding
rubrics_metrics.description: For currently funded NIH grants, supplemental funding may be available through competing revisions to expand a project's scope and administrative supplements to meet unanticipated costs or support career re-entry without a change of scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two main pathways: competing revisions (to expand scope) and administrative supplements (to cover unexpected costs or support specific needs like career re-entry); relevant to current awardees seeking additional support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loan Repayment Programs
rubrics_metrics.description: To retain and recruit professionals in biomedical or biobehavioral careers, NIH repays educational debt in return for a commitment to engage in research relevant to our scientific mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs include extramural and intramural LRP tracks, application guidance (reference letters, institutional certifications), and contacts such as LRP Program Officers and IC Coordinators; aimed at individuals rather than project grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH uses legally binding contracts to acquire goods and services (e.g., research and development work) to support research and research-related activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracts are procurement instruments distinct from grants and cooperative agreements; applicants respond to solicitations when NIH seeks specific goods/services or deliverables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Transactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Though statutory authority, NIH may fund unique legal agreements for a specific function, initiative, program, project, or research. These transactions are not grants, contracts, or cooperative agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for bespoke agreements that do not fit traditional funding mechanisms; terms and requirements vary by initiative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenges and Prizes
rubrics_metrics.description: To address special problems and challenges in biomedical research, NIH competitions and prizes solicit, showcase, and support participants’ transformative solutions and achievements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competitive prize mechanisms intended to stimulate innovation and identify solutions to defined problems; often open to a broad set of participants and intended to reward demonstrable results.
